page: Microsoft Azure M208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for massive memory workloads and compute-heavy parallel processing. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors clocked at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 104 physical cores and 208 vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU feature set includes instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA. For system memory, the instance delivers 2,850.0 GB of RAM, offering approximately 13.7 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage includes 4,398 GB of local SSD capacity, while no discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data demonstrates extreme parallel compute and memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core processing, scoring 187,934.47 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 84,712.92 in PassMark CPU evaluation. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 415.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 191.08 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 689.6 GB/sec, and in-memory key-value processing achieves 153.96 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded throughput represents a performance tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core at 1,147.0 and stress-ng single-core in the bottom 25%.

Given its massive memory footprint, extensive local SSD storage, and top-tier multi-threaded scalability, the M208s_v2 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense consolidation rather than single-threaded tasks. The server is well matched for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive enterprise Redis deployments, heavy distributed data processing, and large-scale relational database engines requiring sustained high memory bandwidth.
